_comment: Sites already carrying the WIN-45 reachability-skip statement shape when check_reachability_skip_shape.py was installed (F29). This file is a RATCHET, not an endorsement: it stops NEW sites from landing. Shrinking it is the work; growing it requires a deliberate edit and a reason. `known_fingerprints` is the authoritative list (see GitHub #204): it carries no line numbers, so an edit above a guard no longer re-reports it as new. `known_sites` is the human-readable file:line index of the same entries, regenerated here and NOT consulted when deciding whether a finding is known.

_ownership.repoint_note: Recorded 2026-09-07 against GitHub #143, which was CLOSED the same day -- by the very act of recording this block, which was #143's ask. The block then named a closed issue and nothing tracked the burn-down; GitHub #204 found that. Worse, a routine `--update-baseline` refresh on 2026-09-18 (commit e6c36ae1) silently DELETED this block altogether, because the generator rewrote the payload from scratch. Both are fixed under #204: the block is restored and repointed at GitHub #229, which is OPEN and owns the burn-down, and --update-baseline now carries operator-authored `_` keys forward instead of dropping them.
_ownership.why_not_permanent: A WIN-45 reachability-skip is a test that records 'blocked' instead of asserting. Every one of these 437 is a test not currently proving what it was written to prove, so the population is real debt rather than an accepted design property -- unlike a genuinely permanent exemption (contrast magnitude_guard_baseline.json's 31 adjudicated entries). The guard is a RATCHET and already stops growth; what it cannot do is make a frozen 437 distinguishable from a healthy 0 to anyone reading CI status instead of this file (DCA 0047).
_ownership.first_tranche: The largest single-file cluster listed above. Taking one file to zero is a bounded, reviewable change and proves the shape is reducible; a global target with no first step is how a burn-down stays at 437.
_ownership.how_to_measure: python tools/gate/check_reachability_skip_shape.py --paths tests --baseline tools/gate/reachability_skip_baseline.json ; the 'known_sites' length in this file IS the number. The same command now also FAILS on a stale entry -- one matching nothing live -- so the file cannot rot in the other direction (GitHub #204).
_ownership.still_blocking_note: TWO NUMBERS, DIFFERENT MEANINGS, AND THE SECOND HAS A SCOPE LIMIT. population_at_repoint (437) counts guard SITES THAT EXIST across 78 files -- that is what the ratchet refuses to grow, and it IS a whole-population figure. still_blocking_measured (13) counts guards that ACTUALLY FIRED, and it was measured over SEVEN files only. DO NOT INFER '424 sites did not block'. That statement appeared in an earlier version of this note and was withdrawn: the other 71 files were never re-run this cycle, so a file that newly began blocking would not appear. The seven measured are the seven the 2026-09-20 census had already found blocking, which makes 13 a CONFIRMATION of the known blockers rather than a fresh sweep of the population. The claim-check gate FAILED this phase over exactly that inference, which is the same shape as this file's own earlier correction, where 437 was being quoted as live debt.
_ownership.still_blocking_method: AUTHORITATIVE ARTIFACT: tests/_runtime/field/win45_census_20260923_AUTHORITATIVE.txt, produced by tests/_runtime/field/win45_derive.sh from the RETAINED raw pytest output in tests/_runtime/field/win45_raw_20260923_021731/ (one file per measured target, kept so a counting bug costs a re-derivation rather than two hours of live UI runs). Counting rule: '^E +Failed: WIN-45 reachability blocked', ONE line per failing test. FOUR counting rules were wrong before this one, all recorded in win45_census.sh's header so they are not re-tried: (1) a per-file timeout recorded as zero; (2) two census loops running concurrently, which gave 4 and 7 blocks for the SAME file; (3) grep -c counting message OCCURRENCES (pytest prints each twice) rather than tests; (4) counting pytest's FAILED short-summary lines, which under -q carry no reason at all and so scored every file 0. Two superseded logs are kept and labelled VOID rather than deleted: win45_census_VOID_contaminated.log (concurrent loops) and win45_census_20260923_021731_VOID_miscounted.log (rule 4). The karen gate FAILED this phase by reading the latter and correctly finding that the cited artifact did not support the claimed figure.

A whole-population sweep is the outstanding work; at the observed per-file cost (up to 20 minutes each) it is roughly a ten-hour run, which is why it was not done in this phase and is recorded here instead of being silently implied.
